quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause your motorcycle to skid.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Always wear hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speed increases, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle goes faster.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: The best way to stay out of trouble while riding is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid high-density traffic areas.
Ride at speeds faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead of your motorcycle. This helps you see and react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may make the other driver move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may make the other driver move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: In California, drivers under 21 cannot legally operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.01 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.01 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: California's legal drinking age is 21. Drivers under 21 cannot operate any motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even small amounts of alcohol can make motorcycle riding unsafe.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard, do NOT:

options.text: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
Adjust your speed accordingly.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always communicate with other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed and change your lane position as needed to handle the hazard safely.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver may not see you. Also, the vehicle can block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT strongly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: Important factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role in determining BAC.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To tell other riders you are near them.
To help others see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
To warn others that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn others that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to tell other drivers you are slowing down in a place where they don't expect it. This is especially important before making a quick turn off a fast road or slowing down suddenly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph. These include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at railroad crossings with flashing lights. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives you the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both the front and rear brakes together when you stop.

questions.question: When it rains, where is the best place to ride your motorcycle?

options.text: On the right side of the lane.
On the edge of the road.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil from cars that has not yet washed away. Ride in the tire tracks made by cars to get better traction.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks up while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then apply it again.

questions.question: A motorcycle can have no more than how many wheels?

options.text: Two wheels
Three wheels
Four wheels

questions.correctAnswerText: Three wheels
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is defined as a motor vehicle with a seat for the rider and no more than three wheels.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what will you likely need to do?

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure changes.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Add a few pounds of air pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest chance of conflict with other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. The biggest danger is when a car turns left in front of a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: No matter which helmet style you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is clean.
Looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible damage.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, position yourself where other drivers can see you best. Be ready to use the clutch and both brakes quickly. Slow down when entering an intersection. Do not speed up or change position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers about what you are doing.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting while turning can cause sudden power changes to the rear wheel, which can cause skidding. If you must shift while turning, shift smoothly to reduce the risk of skidding.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Should be consistently checked by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be consistently checked by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles. Before changing lanes, always turn your head to look for traffic in your blind spot. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal when you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving your signal on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can usually keep control. A locked rear wheel on a straight road does not cause loss of control as long as the motorcycle stays upright.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: When riding on a highway, a motorcyclist should signal _______ before changing lanes.

options.text: Two seconds
Five seconds
10 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Five seconds
questions.explanation: Signal a lane change at least five seconds before you move. This gives other drivers time to see your signal and react safely to your intentions.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or stop sign, stop where indicated. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for approaching traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.
